title: Proposal: Enable the use of other client side scripting languages
body:
It is pretty well understood that JS is not the best solution for client side scripting, and it's popularity is mainly driven by the fact that it is the only choice. That is why we see so many languages which are all transpilled down to JS.

The Problem:
Web developers are forced to use the JS/npm ecosystem purely because there is no other choice (for client side scripting) and the complexity that comes with is a huge strain on productivity and represents a huge learning curve to overcome. Many companies are abandoning JS for TS, Dart, Smalltalk, Scala, Go, Python etc. on the backend for more efficient and newer languages but for client side scripting we are still forced to use JS simply because of the monopoly JS holds on the modern browser. 

JS was never meant to be used for major development projects which has caused many issues and inefficiencies. JS is also much slower / more resource intensive than many other languages and for the IOT devices it presents a major problem. An ESP32 for example is more powerful than a regular PC from 1995 running a Pentium, but it is not powerful enough to run a modern browser because the JS vm is too resource intensive. In the coming years we will see billions of IOT devices sold which need a more efficient client side scripting engine.

Current Alternative:
The only other option right now is forcing page updates from the server side which is inefficient and requires server side rendering, this in many cases is much more resource intensive and costly when it comes to cloud applications that could benefit greatly from the usage of compute cycles of the user.

The Fix:
I believe that the <script> tag should allow for defining other scripting languages (with a fallback option if possible). The script tag already has a type attribute, so it would not be a breaking change to allow defining a different language engine. The browser would then launch whichever interpreter is defined in the script tag (as long as the user has it installed) in a sandboxed VM and expose the same API functions as it does for JS.

In addition to being able to set a script type other than JS it would be beneficial to offer a fallback option as well in case a user does not have the right interpreter or browser support. This can already be done through user agent checking but would be simplified by adding a fallback attribute.

There are already projects working on browser and language options to replace HTML/CSS/JS altogether which would create an even more fractured ecosystem and an even larger mess than what we are already dealing with. Opening up more language options would be a huge benefit and eliminate the need to break off into a separate browser.


I would be happy to hear what other people think of this proposal and maybe there are other suggestions on how to implement this as well.
